# axiolid-evaluate

Analytic and spline curve/surface evaluation, jets, and inversion.

## Overview

The scalar evaluation oracle for parametric geometry (ADR 0012, ADR 0036):
native-domain evaluation of analytic and B-spline curves and surfaces,
derivatives, jets, adaptive flattening, elementary surface inversion,
arc-length evaluation of intrinsic (natural-equation) and elevated curves
and of arc-length chains, arc length and its inverse on any curve,
the section frames of banked curves, the derivatives and certified chord
and derivative bounds of elevated and banked curves in plan distance (over
an intrinsic plan with certified points, #393),
certified chord bounds of the pcurves a section is read through (graphs,
implicit and intrinsic curves, lifted curves and pair sections, #414),
stations (a section frame at a distance along a curve, or along pieces of
curves laid end to end),
and `ReferenceCurveEvaluator`, the reference implementation of the
curve-evaluation contract (ADR 0063). It has no mesh, spatial, measure or
provider dependency, so a parametric consumer gets evaluation without the
`axiolid-reference` umbrella. It favours obvious correctness over speed: no
intrinsics, threading or feature gates.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.3.23 (2026-11-14):

### Added

- `station::FrameLaw::rates`, `FrameRates` and `RateBounds` (#406): certified
  bounds of a section frame law's forward rate, rise, bend toward the lateral
  and up axes and twist over a span, each with its value at the span's middle
  read and that value's error. Frames read by quadrature (ellipses,
  B-splines, offsets beside a line, circle, ellipse or B-spline) have them
  from a certified second derivative of the exact curve; a span across a
  point where their curvature may jump has none. `FrameLaw::bend` and
  `has_bend` now cover frames read by quadrature as well.
